steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On September 30, 2026, both Madrid and the Eastern Time zone will be observing daylight saving time. Madrid will be on CEST (UTC+2) and the Eastern US will be on EDT (UTC-4). The time difference is 6 hours.

5:00 PM (17:00) ET + 6 hours = 11:00 PM (23:00) in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru is in the Peru Time (PET) zone, which is UTC-5. Subtracting 5 hours from 12:00 UTC on July 15, 2026, results in 07:00 on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST (Central European Summer Time) is UTC+2, and Tokyo (JST - Japan Standard Time) is UTC+9. Tokyo is 7 hours ahead of CEST.

June 1, 2026, at 9:00 AM CEST + 7 hours = June 1, 2026, at 4:00 PM (16:00) JST.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PDT (Pacific Daylight Time) is UTC-7. Madrid, Spain, is in the Central European Time zone. On October 11, 2026, Madrid will be observing CEST (Central European Summer Time), which is UTC+2.

The time difference between PDT (UTC-7) and CEST (UTC+2) is 9 hours.

Adding 9 hours to October 11, 2026, at 11:59 PM:
11:59 PM + 1 minute = October 12, 12:00 AM
11:59 PM + 9 hours = October 12, 8:59 AM

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PST (Pacific Standard Time) is UTC-8. Madrid, Spain, in March is on CET (Central European Time), which is UTC+1. The time difference is 9 hours. Adding 9 hours to March 3, 2026, at 11:59 PM results in March 4, 2026, at 8:59 AM.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET (Central European Time) is UTC+1. Los Angeles in February is on PST (Pacific Standard Time), which is UTC-8. The time difference is 9 hours (CET is 9 hours ahead of PST).

Subtracting 9 hours from 10:00 AM on February 2, 2026, results in 1:00 AM on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Japan Standard Time (JST) is UTC+9, and Lima, Peru (PET) is UTC-5. This means JST is 14 hours ahead of Lima.

Subtracting 14 hours from May 5, 2026, at 8:00 AM:
- 8 hours back brings us to 12:00 AM (midnight) on May 5.
- Another 6 hours back brings us to 6:00 PM (18:00) on May 4.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 28, 2026, the United States will still be observing Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7. Spain transitions from Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) to Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) on the last Sunday of October; since October 25, 2026, is that Sunday, Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1) by October 28.

The time difference between PDT (UTC-7) and CET (UTC+1) is 8 hours. 

Adding 8 hours to October 28 at 11:59 PM results in October 29 at 7:59 AM.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 30, 2026, the US will still be observing Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4. Madrid, Spain, will have already switched back to Central European Time (CET) on October 25, 2026, which is UTC+1. This creates a 5-hour time difference.

9:00 AM EDT + 5 hours = 2:00 PM (14:00) CET.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Central European Time (CET) is UTC+1. On October 27, 2026, New York will be observing Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4. The time difference between CET and EDT is 5 hours. Subtracting 5 hours from 18:00 results in 13:00.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in Madrid time, we first identify the time zones in effect on November 2, 2026:

1.  **Pacific Time (PT):** In 2026, Daylight Saving Time in the US ends on November 1. Therefore, on November 2, PT will be Pacific Standard Time (PST), which is **UTC-8**.
2.  **Madrid Time:** In 2026, Daylight Saving Time in Spain ends on October 25. Therefore, on November 2, Madrid will be in Central European Time (CET), which is **UTC+1**.

The time difference between UTC-8 and UTC+1 is **9 hours**.

Adding 9 hours to November 2, 11:59 PM:
- 11:59 PM + 1 hour = 12:59 AM (November 3)
- 12:59 AM + 8 hours = 8:59 AM (November 3)

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On March 20, 2026, the US will be observing Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7), as Daylight Saving Time begins on March 8. Madrid, Spain, will still be observing Central European Time (CET, UTC+1), as European Daylight Saving Time does not begin until March 29. This creates an 8-hour time difference. Adding 8 hours to March 20 at 11:59 PM results in March 21 at 7:59 AM.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On March 25, 2026, Los Angeles will be observing Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7), as US Daylight Saving Time begins on March 8, 2026. Central Europe will still be observing Central European Time (CET, UTC+1), as European Summer Time does not begin until March 29, 2026. 

The time difference between CET (UTC+1) and PDT (UTC-7) is 8 hours. Subtracting 8 hours from 12:00 PM CET results in 4:00 AM PDT.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is given as 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026. 12:00 AM refers to the start of the day.

In October, both Madrid and the US East Coast are observing daylight saving time. Madrid is on Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) and the US East Coast is on Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4).

The time difference is 6 hours (UTC+2 minus UTC-4). Adding 6 hours to 12:00 AM (00:00) on October 12 results in 6:00 AM on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) is equivalent to UTC-12. Madrid, Spain, is in the Central European Summer Time (CEST) zone in October, which is UTC+2. 

The time difference between UTC-12 and UTC+2 is 14 hours. Adding 14 hours to October 9, 23:59, results in October 10, 13:59.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In August, Pacific Time (PT) is in Daylight Saving Time (PDT, UTC-7), and Madrid, Spain is in Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2). The time difference is 9 hours.

12:00 PM (noon) PT + 9 hours = 21:00 (9:00 PM) in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

IST (India Standard Time) is UTC+5:30. Madrid, Spain, will be in CET (Central European Time, UTC+1) on November 10, 2026, as the transition from summer time (CEST) occurs in late October.

The time difference is 4 hours and 30 minutes (IST is ahead of CET).
Subtracting 4 hours and 30 minutes from 11:59 PM (23:59) on November 10 results in 7:29 PM (19:29) on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Nepal Standard Time (NPT) is UTC+5:45, and Lima, Peru (PET) is UTC-5. The time difference is 10 hours and 45 minutes (Nepal is ahead).

Subtracting 10 hours and 45 minutes from 5:00 PM (17:00) on April 2, 2026:
17:00 - 10 hours = 07:00
07:00 - 45 minutes = 06:15

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 6, 2026, Adelaide will be observing Australian Central Daylight Time (ACDT, UTC+10:30), as daylight saving typically begins on the first Sunday of October. Madrid will be observing Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2), as daylight saving ends on the last Sunday of October.

The time difference is 8 hours and 30 minutes (10:30 - 2:00). Subtracting 8 hours and 30 minutes from 10:00 AM on October 6 results in 1:30 AM on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney, Australia, will be on Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST, UTC+10) on October 3, 2026, as Daylight Saving Time does not begin until the following day (Sunday, October 4). Madrid, Spain, will be on Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2).

The time difference is 8 hours (Sydney is 8 hours ahead of Madrid).

18:00 (Sydney time) - 8 hours = 10:00 (Madrid time).

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
